endorsements.quote: Large‐scale observational studies and/or RCTs with long‐term follow‐up will be required to understand if the use of CADe truly contributes to health economy and patient care.

unlisted_practices: Health-care delivery systems and authorities should evaluate the cost-effectiveness of CADe to support its use in clinical practice.
Health-care delivery systems and authorities should evaluate the cost-effectiveness of CADx to support its use in clinical practice.
Undertake a broad range of high-quality cost-effectiveness research to understand whether AI implementation benefits populations and societies in different health-care systems.
Health-care delivery systems and authorities should consider clinical benefits, cost-effectiveness, or other formal health technology assessment of AI tools to support use in clinical practice.
Design AI reimbursement carefully, avoiding per-use payment that may cause overuse of AI, to improve patient outcomes while maximizing cost-effectiveness and equity.
Adopt practices that reduce medical-legal risk for CADx, such as systematic photo documentation or video recording of endoscopic features supporting diagnoses and management decisions.
Provide financial incentives to physicians who utilize CADx to support its spread in clinical practice.

screen.reason: This is a World Endoscopy Organization (WEO) position statement providing guidance and recommendations on implementing AI (CADe/CADx) in colonoscopy.
